findings.title: Async legacy write derives context from cancelled request context
findings.body: Create (and Delete line 110, Update line 135, DeleteCollection line 163) spawns `go func()` then does `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`, where `ctx` is the incoming request context. The method returns immediately, the apiserver cancels the request context, and any child derived from it is cancelled immediately. The background Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection will therefore almost always run with a cancelled parent and fail/timeout, so the legacy copy is never kept in sync despite mode 3 promising best-effort legacy writes. Use a detached context like `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or `context.Background()` for the async work.

findings.title: Update re-invokes UpdatedObjectInfo for legacy causing divergence
findings.body: Update forwards the same `objInfo` to `Storage.Update` and then asynchronously to `Legacy.Update`. Each store calls `UpdatedObject(ctx, old)` with its own different `old` object. If the transformer is not idempotent or depends on old resourceVersion/spec, the two stores compute different new objects or one fails with conflict. The previous implementation fetched the updated object once and reused it via `updateWrapper` so legacy got the storage result. Legacy should be written with the object returned from storage, not by re-executing user logic against stale legacy state, otherwise storage and legacy diverge.

findings.title: Delete success records object name as kind metric label
findings.body: On successful storage delete the code calls `recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, ...)` where `name` is the object name like `foo`, while the error path and all other methods pass `options.Kind`. The `kind` label will get unbounded high-cardinality values (one series per object name), exploding Prometheus series and breaking dashboards/alerts that expect kind. It should be `options.Kind`.

findings.title: DeleteCollection legacy result recorded as storage metric
findings.body: The background goroutine for DeleteCollection calls `recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` for the `Legacy.DeleteCollection` result instead of `recordLegacyDuration`. Legacy latency and errors are attributed to the storage histogram and legacy metrics are never emitted for this method, corrupting SLOs and hiding legacy failures. All other async paths correctly call `recordLegacyDuration`.

findings.title: Create/Update storage errors recorded as legacy metrics
findings.body: When `Storage.Create` fails the code calls `recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)` and Update does the same on line 129 for `Storage.Update` failure. A storage failure is counted as a legacy failure with the storage start time, so storage error rate/latency is missing and legacy error rate is inflated. The error paths should call `recordStorageDuration` like Delete and DeleteCollection do.

findings.title: Delete discards per-request logger when installing context
findings.body: Delete builds `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)` but then does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `log`. Downstream storage calls and any `klog.FromContext` logs lose name/kind/method fields, inconsistent with Create/Get/List/Update/DeleteCollection which install the enriched logger, harming correlation and debugging.

findings.title: Async legacy failures are never logged
findings.body: All four background legacy writes only call `recordLegacyDuration`/`recordStorageDuration` and drop the error. There is no `log.Error` with name/kind/UID. Operators will not see why the legacy safety copy failed in logs, unlike the previous synchronous code which logged legacy errors. At minimum log the async legacy error with identifying fields.

findings.title: Mode3 tests do not verify async legacy dual-write
findings.body: Mode3 write tests return immediately after the synchronous storage call and never wait for the background legacy goroutine (no sleep/Eventually/AssertCalled). Delete and DeleteCollection tests set no legacy expectation at all, and legacy and storage share the same `*mock.Mock` so `Create/Update/Delete` calls cannot be attributed to a store. Tests pass even if legacy is never written (masking the cancelled-context bug above) and are flaky if the goroutine runs after the test finishes and hits an unexpected mock call.
